0.
0.1 This

FOREWORD

Indian Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 13 March 1987, after the draft finalized by the Special Alloys SecConal Committee had been approved by the Structural and Metals Division Council. 0.2 This standard has been prepared for rationalizing the requirements of magnetic materials which are often referred to as `commercially pure' or `magnetically soft' irons. This material is generally available in a wide variety of forms, such as, slabs, billets, ingots, forgings, hot rolled bars or as flat rolled sheets and strips. 0.3 The main applications for these materials are in dc relays, loudspeakers, electromagnets, maguetic clutches, brakes, parts for magnetic circuits in instruments and control apparatus as well as Ibr pole pieces and other parts for generators and motors. 0.4 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS : 2-1260*. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off values should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

1. SCOPE
standard covers requirements of cold rolled soft magnetic iron strips primarily intended for electromagnetic purposes, such as relay yoke, armature and the like ofe!ectrical machinery and apparatus. 2. SUPPLY

5. PHYSICAL

CONDITION

5.1 The material shall be uniform in composition and micro and macro structure, sound and free from physical defect or flaw both externally and internally.
5.2 The strips as received shall be smooth waviness, bow, bend or buckle. and flat and quite free from

5.3 Material in coil shall be uniformly treated and of uniform hardness and characteristics such that it shall uncoil free from waviness. 5.4 The surface of the maferial shall be bright, clean and smooth, and shall be free from any physical imperfections, such as rust, dirt, scale, The surFace shall scabs, pitting, blisters, seems, heavy score marks, etc. be suitable for electroplating. 6. PROPERTIES

7.1 Coercive Force -The coercive force shall be determined on a test piece after annealing at 800�C for 3 h under atmospheric conditions of controlled dccarborization and cooling in the furnace at a maximum cooling rate of SO'Cjh or as per manufacturers recommendations. The annealed test piece shall be tested on a `FORSTER' type coercimeter or conventional ballistic flux meter method. 10. SAMPLING

10.1 One representative sample for a lot shall he taken for tensile testing. A lot shall consist of 30 tonnes or less of strip of the same If the lot consists quality rolled to the same thickness and condition. of more than one heat, samples from each heat shall he tested. 10.2 For hardness, grain size, bend test and other magnetic properties one sample from each lot of 5 tonnes or part thereof shall be taken. 11. RETESTS 11.1 Should any of 11~e test pieces first selected fail to pass any of the two further samples &all he selected tests specified in this standard, from the same lot for testing in respect of each failure. Should the test pieces from both the additional samples pass, the material represented by the test samples shall be deemed to comply with the recjuiremcnis of that particular test. Should the test pieces from represented IJy either of. these additional samples fail, the material the test sample. shall Ix dcerned as not confn~ming to this standard.

12. PACKING 12.1 Each strip/coil type rust-preventing alkali solution.
shall be treated on both sides with oil, which can be easily washed non-hardening w,th aqueous

12.2 The mass of each case shall be mutually agreed between the The material shall be well protected purchaser and the manufacturer. from damages and corrosion during transit. The bundle shall be wrapped with hessian water-proof cloth and tied with hoop iron. External packing shall be done with strong wooden cases or crates to prevent damage to the edges. 13. MARKING

13.1 The following shall be legibly marked on the top of each bundle or package of strips or as shown on a tag attached to each coil:
a ) Manufacturer's b) Quality/grade, c) Product dimensions, 8 name and trade-mark,

IS : 11946- 1987 d) Cast or identification mark by which the strip may be traced to cast or casts from which they are made, e) Net and gross weight, f) Date of despatch. 13.2 The material may also be marked with the Standard Mark. and

NOTE -The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well-defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and Standard marked products are supervired by BIS and operated by the producer. also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.
